utterances.text: Did you investigate, for example, various allegations that had been made by international organisations against NATO and the NATO bombing campaign? Did you investigate that?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: There was no support for that, was there?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Not my team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, other teams in the CCIU, are you aware that they investigated the various allegations that had been made against the NATO bombing campaign in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: CCIU had all war crimes cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes. And of course in your capacity as a war crimes investigator, you, no doubt, were aware that various international organisations, for example Human Rights Watch, but as well as the Serb government themselves were alleging that NATO committed war crimes by bombing Kosovo? You heard of that, of course?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: As an experienced investigator. And in your team meetings in the CCIU, what investigations took place in relation to the NATO air strikes in Kosovo? Do you remember or not?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: But of course you remember investigations conducted against the KLA?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes, because that was mainly the cases I had in my team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember if anybody in particular was encouraging you to investigate allegations against the KLA?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No. I -- we -- I as a team leader got the cases that the suspects was the KLA from my unit leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Yes. Now you're training police officers in Bosnia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: We are inspecting and mentoring the leaders in the police in Bosnia, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And of course before you came to Macedonia, you had trained as a police officer in Norway.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: A very good police force, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And that's a very unbiased opinion, but it's a very good police force.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And of course you know that as a basic rule of police investigation that police officers keep a police notebook with them when they conduct investigations. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters please ask speakers to speak slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I am grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: A notebook that they keep in which they record any investigations which they consider relevant. That's normal practice, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And of course those notebooks and those notes can contain a whole variety of information other than information which may make its way eventually on a written witness statement. It contains information which the investigator considers relevant to the case.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: But where are your notes? Where are your original notes of these statements?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Original notes? I don't know where they are now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: That's not good practice, is it, if you don't know where they are. Didn't you keep them? Weren't they stored? Weren't they preserved?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: The handwritten you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your original notes. Your notebook.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No. I think it was destroyed when I went from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: And of course you accept that's bad practice, isn't it, for police notes to be destroyed when there is an ongoing criminal investigation. That's bad practice, isn't it, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah, but everything was written in the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: It's very bad practice that the original notes made by a police officer in relation to an ongoing investigation are not preserved. It's not something you would advise your Bosnian colleagues to do, is it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When did you leave your mission in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: June -- June 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And from that time until the present, I take it that you've had no further responsibilities with regard to any investigation of matters concerning war crimes in Kosovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've been a police officer for over 20 years now, have you not, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes. I graduated the academy in 1983, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So that would be over 20 years.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during that time, if I understand your testimony correctly, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you've been in a position on more than one occasion to not only monitor but also mentor your fellow officers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, right now you're engaged in efforts concerning monitoring, mentoring, and inspecting middle and upper management in Bosnia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please make pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... No, not in the fields. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the work that you're doing at this juncture is training your fellow officers how to do their job.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The work that you did before Kosovo, was that work in the field?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Work in the field and also in investigations, both.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in terms of investigations, the training that you received with regard to investigations is training which you received in Norway?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And on the job? And on the job?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: And on the job, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, investigations I take it when you were engaged in investigations concerning the United Nations, it's a little bit different than the investigations you were involved in concerning war crimes in Kosovo. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you were involved in investigations concerning war crimes in Kosovo, there were a series of factors you had to take into account in order to make a determination as to whether or not the information that you were getting was complete and accurate. True?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What were some of those factors, sir?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: We had to take care of names and everything like that so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you have to be able to take care of names and everything like that, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: When we did the investigations we had to be careful who we gave to information to with names and everything. So like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that because you find the names in Kosovo to be somewhat unique?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No. It was information this witness gave to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Apart from this particular factor, the factor of names that you had to be careful with, were there any other factors that were unique with regard to your investigative practices in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: These cases we had there was murder cases and I was not used to investigate so many murder cases at home in Norway.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you were not used to investigating so many murder cases, are you telling us that this is the first time you were involved in actively being a homicide investigator in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: As a leader, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Had you previously been involved in homicide investigations?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What did you find the distinctions of being a leader as opposed to being someone who merely investigated a homicide?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: The difference, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: If you are a leader you have to have an overview of everything, as a leader of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a leader, of course, you also need to make a determination that all of the people that are working for your team, as it were --

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- are using the same methodology that you're using. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you of course imposed upon your team a methodology of information retrieval, did you not?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you've told us with some of that methodology was with regard to information retrieval, if I'm not mistaken, and that is in terms of the taking of statements. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, before you became a team leader in Kosovo, having been an experienced police officer prior to that time, you were well aware of the importance of statements being taken being as close to being verbatim as possible. True?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't know the word "verbatim." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Word for word, that the very words that the individuals you were speaking to are being tracked, taken down, and memorialised.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I still don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Let me try another way. That each word that the witness used was a word that you somehow memorialised, you took down. Correctly?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You didn't, for example, tell anybody in your team to engage in interpretation of what witnesses were saying, did you?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If they did do that, that of course would be a deviation from the an investigative process that you knew about. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be incorrect?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be a wrong thing to do?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In this particular matter, when you spoke with Mr. Ademaj on the 13th of September -- am I correct on the date?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that's the date that you have contained in your chronology?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I have my log here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that's the way you know that's the correct date?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have no independent date of that memory, do you?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I remember it now because it read it earlier today when I stated this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say you remember looking at the piece of paper, that's what's giving you solace there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You used a particular technique, as I understand it, which is first of all you told the gentleman what your investigation was about. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, is that information that you wrote down in your police notebook?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. I had the reports in my mind, what I was going to tell him about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So there is no record as you sit here today of what precisely you told this gentleman you were there to speak to him about. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Only my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your report indicates the preface, the beginning of what you told this man, why you were there?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: When I took the statement, I wrote it in my pen first, notes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that. What you've told us is when you take a statement you break it down into four distinct areas. First of all you tell the person you're interviewing what this is about, why you're there to talk to this person.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: He tells his story.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What he has to tell me about. He tells you his story. Right?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And then if there's some questions after you've heard his story, you ask those questions.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the very first part, when you're discussing with him why you're there interviewing him. Did you write that down, what you said to him?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. When you were speaking with this gentleman, is the information that is contained in what is now P86, identified as 0323-0952, the second statement?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that information information that you were writing down in pencil?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As he was speaking to you?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes. I wrote notes about it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And is that the information that you then had available to put in the very first statement that you've discussed, which would be P85?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I took the notes the same day of course, but I couldn't have it in the same report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the second report, you've told us here that you've asked him directly the question: "Is (redacted) lying or are you lying?" Do you remember telling us that?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes. I asked him about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is that information --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers please make pauses between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. If they're going to be -- if there are going to be more questions on this report it might be good to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise. I do apologise. That would be fine. And I would request there be a redaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There will be a redaction Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You came to Kosovo and worked there on this investigation for one year between the years 2000 and 2001.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You came to Kosovo as a highly experienced police officer.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you began work, you worked for the CCIU, which was a creature, a creation, of UNMIK, was it not?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who directed the investigations conducted by the CCIU that you carried out as a team leader?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who was ahead you of you in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: The unit leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: When I came to the unit it was a Swedish and then one American took over and then a third -- second American was the command when I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I direct this question through to the bench across the way. Are the names of any of those individuals in any way sensitive? If they are I shall go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Can you name them, please.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I only remember one, American. Funteller [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I think his name was Funteller, American.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you work on this investigation at the same time as Mr. Lehtinen?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Mr. Lehtinen?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Ole Lehtinen?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you attend regular meetings of the investigation team?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, aren't the words understandable to you? Did you go to meetings of the investigation team of which you were the leader. Do you understand that question?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: If we have had meetings about this case, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Of course. I'm only interested in this case for the moment.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: We didn't have meetings about this case, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You didn't have one meeting in the whole year you were engaged in this investigation about this case with members of your team? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No, because I was involved with this team alone -- this case alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How many members of your team were there?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Different numbers but between five and six I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that for 12 months the five or six of you never sat down in a room together to discuss the investigation?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: We were talking of course about the case, but we didn't have proper meetings just to talk about the case, no. Of course we talked together about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was everything done by members of your team reported to you, as far as you were aware?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah. About this case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm only interested in this case, Mr. Birkeland. If I ask you about others, I shall tell you. So it's only this case I'm interested in. When you were to come in due course to interview Isak Musliu you did so as a witness and not as a suspect, did you not?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah. I took a statement as a witness, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who made the decision to speak to him as a witness rather than as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: As I remember, I talked to my unit leader about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: He was American. I don't -- this was the American I can't remember his name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And was it he, this unnamed American, who made the decision that he should be -- Musliu should be seen as a witness rather than as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes. I remember we took the decision together, me and him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So you were party to that decision, part of that decision. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I want to ask you about your approach to this investigation as an investigator. From your point of view, Mr. Birkeland, was this investigation an objective search for the truth?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you looking to find out the truth or were you seeking to prove a fact? Which was it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I was investigating to find the truth, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let's be clear. I want to find out, if I can, from you, sir, what your starting point was, you see, how you approached your investigation. Did you approach it from the basis that there was a camp, a prison camp, or let's see if we can prove there was a camp. What was your approach, would you say?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: When I started the case, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mmm.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I started the case with the information I got and alternate information, I got information about a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I don't know if it's because you're not understanding me or you're not prepared to answer my questions. I'm this trying to find out your approach as the senior investigator on the ground. Was your starting point that there was a camp or were you open-minded about it? Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you understand what open-minded means?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Gather the facts together and then draw a conclusion. That's being open-minded, isn't sit?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Being closed minded is: I'm out to prove something. Do you follow me?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, which was your approach, the first or the second?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: The first.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know what a leading question is?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What is a leading question?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: If I get a question that can be answered in two ways, in a way. When the question leads to an answer that maybe is not the correct answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid precisely the reverse of what I understand a leading question to be. I suggest a leading question is a question that suggests the answer within the question. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: The answer in the question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, let me give you an example. When you met Xheladin Ademaj, you told us this afternoon you asked him if the camp could be in a place called Lapusnik. You put the location of the camp to Ademaj, didn't you? That, I suggest, is a leading question. Do you agree you did that?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes, I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you think it's valuable and worthwhile as an investigator to put leading questions to witnesses?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No. While we're on the subject of him, Mr. Ademaj that is, let me ask you one or two more questions about the meeting you had with him. I wonder if you've still got it there, Mr. Birkeland. It's the document now our P86, which is the supplement continuation form 0323-0952. Have you got it there?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it customary in investigations from --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Oh, I'm grateful to Mr. Guy-Smith. I think we are about to mention a name. Perhaps it's sensible to go into private session. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: There are two documents we've provided copies of. These are already in evidence, of course; these are the witness statements of Mr. Musliu. For reference purposes they are Prosecution Exhibits 32 and 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I wonder if you could just put them literally side by side, Mr. Birkeland. It may help you to answer my questions. First of all, the date. They both occurred on the 24th of May, 2001. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: They're both headed with that date. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: They're both headed at the same time, 10.20 a.m. is that right?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As you give evidence to us this evening, do you have any independent recollection of this interview?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I remember the first interview, which I signed, but I don't remember the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The first interview that you signed is 03231634. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You don't remember the other one?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I remember that my German colleague was going to take this statement, but I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. On how many occasions do you say Isak Musliu was interviewed by your investigation team?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I think this was the two only times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You see, I'm going to suggest to you that it was only once and what's happened is two documents have been prepared out of one interview that lasted some four hours. Now, is that possible?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No, it was taken two statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why are they both headed the same day and the same time if there are two of them?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: They were taken the same day but not the same -- but not the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, they say they were started on the same time. Look at the document.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Probably the German put the same date because we went there and I started my interview that day -- that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who is the German? Sorry?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: The name is Frank Sparla who took the second statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And was he sitting next to you?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I can't remember if he was present when I took my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why would two investigators be taking two statements?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Because this was two different cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right. So we need to look at the content, therefore, do we? Let's look, then, at 1634 first of all. This seems to be an interview during which a number of names of disappeared were being put to Musliu. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you were doing this, were you?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He was being interviewed as a witness, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right. The entirety of the content really of that statement, or rather the most of it was about names of disappeared. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But it also talks about his service as a UCK soldier in Drenica, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah, I asked him some questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It talks about him being a team leader in Lapusnik, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It talks about his team in the beginning having 11 soldiers and at the most 15 to 16, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It talks about in August 1998 becoming a deputy commander of the 121st Brigade, does it not?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Then it talks in December 1998 of him becoming a commander of the UCK military police in the Nerodimlja area until June of 1999, does it not?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It then asks him about a number of named individuals, does it not?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, this was done treating him as a witness. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In that same interview that treated him as a witness, you asked this question: "In the summer of 1998 you was a team leader in Lapusnik. Do you know anything about a house used as a prison in this area?"

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why did you ask him that question?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Just for information to get facts about --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a witness?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He answered: "Lapusnik fighting area was divided into 3-4 parts. I was serving in one of them. In my area there were no prisons. I've not heard about any prisons." Yes?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So this interview conducted by you that was part of a different investigation, as you've just told us, went on to ask him this question: "A prison in Lapusnik had a commander called Haradin Balay [sic], nickname Shala. Another soldier in this prison was Agim Murtezi, nickname Murizzi [sic]" --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have to object. He did not testify that this was part of a different investigation. He testified that the two interviews were related to different investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Which investigation was this interview related to, Mr. Birkeland? Disappeared people? Lapusnik? Both? Or something else? Which?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: This was information I wanted to have in my case for missing persons and --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Pardon? I didn't hear the last part of your sentence.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: For missing persons in this area. That's why I wanted information of all these persons here, if he knew them, and everything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: But it also seemed to be about Lapusnik, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes, he was a leader there. We wanted to ask him if he know anything about this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He told you he was one of a number of fighting groups in Lapusnik, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He also told you that there was more than one person called Shala, didn't he? You won't find it there, Mr. Birkeland, you didn't write that down. But he told you that, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And he told you somebody called Shala was a man called Rushdi Karpuzi, known as Shala. Do you remember that, Mr. Birkeland?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If he did tell you that, would there be any reason why you didn't write that down?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Of course it wouldn't be the case that you didn't want to hear answers like that; that wouldn't be a reason for not writing it down, would it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I wrote -- I writed down every information I get in my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You see the trouble with that answer, Mr. Birkeland, is we shall never see your original notes of this interview, will we? Will we?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No. My original notes is not here, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you destroy your original notes?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Who did?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is it good police practice to destroy original notes?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's thoroughly bad practice, isn't it, Mr. Birkeland?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Help Their Honours, please. Why is the original of this interview not in existence today? Help us.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't know. I was not in Kosovo when this was destroyed, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: How do you know they were destroyed, then? Who told you?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No one had told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why have you used the word "destroyed" three times today?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Because if the notes were not destroyed I think they would have followed this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: They would have followed the case, not the maker of the notes, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: They would probably follow the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. Let's look at the other interview that's now conducted by your German colleague for a moment or two. First of all, did you stay around while this took place?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't remember this -- the statement, so I don't think I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So which would have come first, yours or your German colleague's?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I think mine was first.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So you would have said something to Mr. Musliu like, Well, I'm going to leave you now but my colleague has some more questions for you. Would that be it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you assure -- tell Mr. Musliu whether he was still being seen now by your colleague as a witness or was he now a suspect?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I presume that my German colleague told that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, it's a fair assumption from the very first lines of the second statement which begin with the words: "I understand I will be questioned as a witness." It goes on, the heading: "The police officer from the CCIU in Pristina, dealing with war crimes, missing persons and these things explained to me it is possible in the future I will be questioned as a suspect... That depends on further investigations..." Now, you didn't say that to him.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That must have been your colleague?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of interest, why isn't that paragraph with that understanding as a condition, as it were, of the interview at the head of the witness statement you took?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In this second interview which you have in front of you, our Exhibit P33, he is asked some questions about the disappearance, is he not, of a man called Bungu, or rather, about a man called Bungu not the disappearance of. That's in the first line of it. Have you got that?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah. Bafti Bungu. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. He in this statement talks about the village he lived in. Correct? This is Mr. Musliu. I live in Recak, where I was born, I have a son and a daughter, I'm a KPS officer.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It deals with March of 1998 coming to Kosovo, being a KLA soldier, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: A team leader of a fighting KLA group for three or three and a half months in the area of Lapusnik --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting is on his feet again so I shall stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness has testified that he was not present at this interview. All he is do is what we can do, which is read the document, and therefore I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "Then I became deputy commander --" Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, no, I was asking, not leading you on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Well, Your Honours, I was going to ask this witness in connection with which investigation this statement was taken. This witness became the team leader of this investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's fine. If you've moving on, we'll then go to that question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Birkeland, it goes on, doesn't it: "In March 1998..." it deals with him coming lack to Lapusnik and him becoming deputy commander of the KLA brigade. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now over the page. Count with me. Four paragraphs down beginning with the words "it is possible." "It is possible that some persons/KLA members have been arrested during the war because of cooperating with the Serbs. These people were not arrested like real prisoners, as far as I know. They have been kept, I would say. We had no KLA prisons or detention centers. I know nothing about that." Mr. Birkeland, in which investigation was this statement being taken?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: It was in the investigation Frank Sparla was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Into what?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: It was a case he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Into what?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What case?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Birkeland --

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Which case this was?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Please, please. Just think about your answers, will you. This is about Lapusnik, isn't it? That's what he's talking about, this trial, this indictment. This was one interview. These weren't two separate interviews and they've been split into two documents, haven't they?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: They are two separate interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No. There was one interview that has been split into two documents, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I want to ask you why that was done because I suggest you know why that was done, because you became the leader of this team. That's why I'm asking you. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: This was taken as two separate witness statements, as I remember so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We can leave that now. Just one or two more things I want to ask you about. During the course of your investigation work in Kosovo in that 12-month period, did you become aware of Serb infiltration into the KLA?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember that I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not one example?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you become aware of the use by the Serb authorities of informants who infiltrated the KLA?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not one example?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know what an agent provocateur is?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Somebody who infiltrates an organisation, provokes the committing of criminal conduct, and then reports on the people who commit it. It's an agent provocateur. Were you aware of the use of any such persons by the Serb authorities during your police work in Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- in the year 2000, 2001?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you agree for the most part in relation to the investigation into the matters concerning Lapusnik, you were dealing with ordinary people, Kosovar Albanians, members of a rural community? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your 12 months, did you come across any information or material regarding the settling of old scores, the seeking of revenge, one member of a community upon another? Come across anything like that, Mr. Birkeland?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Can you say that question once more.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Of course I can. Did you come across in your investigations information or material that what might have been going on, among other things, was the settling of old scores, the taking of revenge, one member of the community against another?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: What do you mean by old scores?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Old scores. Well, let's just use the word "revenge." Everyone understands what revenge means. Come across anything like that?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah, of course I heard it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you come across anyone suggesting to you that there might be political motivations for the making of allegations against people in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah, we also heard about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you investigate such things as thoroughly as we investigated everything else, Mr. Lehtinen [sic]?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: That can't be for me, but if it is I'm busy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's not -- the witness is not Mr. Lehtinen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Birkeland, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: We'll wait for the phone to die.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you want me to repeat the question, Mr. Birkeland?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I missed it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, it's a phone that I received from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Well, there you are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a plea of guilty and of mitigation --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's a plea of guilty and of mitigation. It's not my phone, but I do have possession of one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: It's an old defence, Your Honour. It never works. I'll never do anyone a good turn again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The question was this, Mr. Birkeland: Did you come across anyone suggesting to you that there might be political motivation for the making of allegations against certain people in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Not as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Not as you can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: If Your Honours forgive me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm grateful to somebody.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One more question on these two interviews and it's as it were a question of mechanics, Mr. Birkeland. Could you just have them open and it's the last pages of both. And to be specific for our reference purposes if you would be good enough to have 03231635 and 03231641 open as well. These are the final signature pages of the interview or interviews of Musliu. Okay?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: On the local version or on the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: English. I'm looking at English because I don't understand Albanian when I look at it, you see. First of all, the first question on the English versions is: Is there any reason you can think of why the finish -- the completion time and date is not inserted there?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No, I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, if you turn to the Albanian versions of both, namely 1638 and 1645, can you see that each of those versions, Albanian now, bear a date?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why are the dates different? Can you help us?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Have you got Mr. Ademaj's statement there in front of you still? I think it's on its way.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I have it here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Has that got a finish time and date on it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My very last question. Back to Lapusnik, in general. In the course of your investigations, Mr. Birkeland, did you look into the question of KLA deployment in the village of Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Does it follow from that answer that you do not know how many different units there were operating in Lapusnik in the spring and summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: No -- I don't -- I can't remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I can't remember. No. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Which of those three? No or I can't remember?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I cannot remember it at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Birkeland, you testified that it was your practice when conducting interviews that you would have the person -- you would tell the person what the investigation was about, you would let them tell their story, and then you would follow -- you would ask any follow-up questions if necessary.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would turn your attention to the interview that you conducted with Isak Musliu and the report which is -- it's Prosecution Exhibit P32.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if the usher could make sure that he has that before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you have that document before you now?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recall if you followed that practice in this case when you interviewed Mr. Musliu, that is, told him what the investigation was about, let him tell his story, and then ask questions?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah, I think I did the same also here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I would draw your attention to the file number which appears on the document. Can you see what that is, what the file number is on that document. It's in the upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you still have your log of the investigation that you were working on in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is there a file number on that log?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The same file number?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, could you look for a moment at the interview that you say you were not a part of, which is Prosecution Exhibit P33. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is there a file on that document?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: It is 2001 and 00015.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So it's a different file number?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Does that mean it's a different case?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: It's a different case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That other interview that you did not participate in with Isak Musliu with a different file number relates, as you've already testified to, the disappearance of Bafti Bungu.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you recall if that name, Bafti Bungu, came up at all in your investigation of disappearances related to Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You can't remember the name coming up or you can't remember either way?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I remember the name, but I cannot remember if it came up in my case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If you could take a moment -- look at your log. Would your log refresh your recollection about whether the name came up? Looking at the log, do you see that name anywhere on the log?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes, I see his name. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you know that if -- do you recall -- did this missing person case have any connection to Lapusnik? Do you recall either way?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, one final question. Looking again at the two interviews pertaining to the two different cases which are Prosecution Exhibits P32 and P33, you were asked a question or two about the last page of the Albanian version of these two interviews. Were the signatures on the last pages of the Albanian versions put there when the witness -- I'm sorry. I'm jumping the gun here.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: I see ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you have them in front of you, P32 and P33? The last page -- the last pages of the Albanian versions. I don't know if the usher can be of assistance on this. You have a lot of papers now in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I apologise for the confusion. We put too much paper in front of you. Now you have the last pages of the Albanian versions of P32 and P33 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You testified previously that oftentimes the interview would be conducted, the report of the interview would be typed up, and at a later date, sometimes some days later, the document would be reviewed by the witness and signed.

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, looking at the last pages of these two separate interviews, are the signatures here of the -- signatures of the witness on these last pages?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes. It is the same signature I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it's the signature of the witness?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Musliu?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the dates are later than the date of the interview, which was the 24th of May. It appears that one is the 25th of May and one is the 30th of May. Does that accord with what you see?

utterances.speaker: KAARE BIRKELAND
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Birkeland, that is the end of your questioning. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance and your assistance and you're now free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber itself will now adjourn. As all will be aware, tomorrow is a plenary sitting of the Chamber so this trial will not continue and it will continue on Thursday at 2.15. Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may ask for some indulgence, I will be but a minute. It relates to a filing yesterday which was jointly submitted by the Defence teams in this case in relation to the matter of proofing. Your Honour, as a matter of clarification perhaps matters were misstated somewhat, accidentally. The correct position is in relation to paragraph 3(D) of the Defence reply, and I've just spoken earlier to my learned friend Mr. Cayley, it was thought appropriate to bring it to your attention. It was said that in our reply that the Office of the Prosecutor had no recollection of how various answers were triggered or the context in which the witness volunteered an identification of Fatmir Limaj in the second of five proofing sessions. Your Honours, Mr. Cayley was courteous and proper enough, as always, to speak to Mr. Mansfield and myself about this matter before we came into court. And in actual fact, what Mr. Cayley had said to Mr. Mansfield and I in relation to the matters that were being discussed is that when the witness is speaking to Mr. Cayley about this unnamed commander we heard about yesterday, he was asked to give a description. And at that point, Mr. Cayley told us that the witness immediately directed the Prosecutor to a web site, stating there was a photograph on the web site. So Your Honours, it's just a matter of courtesy so that we don't misstate what was told to us by our learned friends. So that was the reason why I rose and bothered you some more today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Khan. We will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of December, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
